The image presents two line charts, each displaying the relationship between time (in years) on the x-axis and various financial metrics on the y-axis. The charts share a common x-axis, spanning from 1995 to 2020.

Both charts have two y-axes: the left axis represents the "IWF Fiskalindex" (IMF Fiscal Index), and the right axis represents different metrics for each chart. The left chart's right axis measures "Schuldenquote Gesamtstaat" (General Government Debt Ratio), while the right chart's right axis measures "Schuldenquote Zentralstaat" (Central Government Debt Ratio).

The left chart displays three data series: the IWF Fiskalindex (blue triangles), Schuldenquote Gesamtstaat (blue line), and another series (purple line) that closely follows the blue line. The IWF Fiskalindex remains relatively stable around 1, with some fluctuations. The Schuldenquote Gesamtstaat starts at around 60 in 1995, increases to approximately 80 by 2010, and then rises sharply to nearly 120 by 2020.

The right chart also shows three data series: the IWF Fiskalindex (blue triangles), Schuldenquote Zentralstaat (blue line), and another series (purple line). The IWF Fiskalindex remains relatively stable around 1. The Schuldenquote Zentralstaat begins at around 40 in 1995, decreases to approximately 35 by 2000, and then fluctuates before rising to around 60 by 2020.

DESCRIPTION: The image contains two line charts displaying financial metrics over time, with the left chart showing the General Government Debt Ratio and the right chart showing the Central Government Debt Ratio, both in relation to the IMF Fiscal Index.
